title: rust-mutants touched v1
description: What the guards of an instrumented tree recorded on the run that verified its baseline: which of each target's tests reached which mutation, which sites were reached where nothing named a test, and which targets said nothing this run can route by. A target absent from `targets` and named in `limitations` is one every test of which reaches every mutation in it. `narrowing` says which mutants the tree could record anything about, without which an absence in `bodies` or `infected` says nothing at all. `items` is the item catalog an `entered` index names.

targets.description: Every target whose guards recorded, by identity.

limitations.description: Why a target the run built is not in `targets`, as `<limitation>:<target>`.

narrowing.description: Which of the records above are facts about which mutant. Every record here is an absence saying something, and an absence says nothing unless the tree carried the call that would have broken it.

compared.description: Every mutant whose guard evaluates its two branches, by dense catalog index, so `infected` is a fact about it.

bodies.description: The marker each mutant's branch proof rests on, by dense catalog index, keeping only the markers the instrumenter wrote; a body inside a guard's own site takes none.

items.description: Every item of every file the tree instrumented, by item index: the catalog an index in `entered` names. An item whose `measurable` is false is one whose body the compiler may evaluate at compile time, so nothing records entering it and an absence from `entered` says nothing about it.

item.description: One item of an instrumented file whose body a test can enter.

index.description: The dense item index an entry marker names, which is the item's position in `items`.

package.description: The package whose unit compiled the file.

path.description: The workspace-relative path with forward slashes.

name.description: The item as a reader writes it, which is what a mutant inside it names as its `item`.

span.description: The bytes the whole item covers in the pristine file, attributes and signature included.

body.description: The bytes its body covers in the pristine file.

measurable.description: Whether entering the body is something the guards record; a `const fn`, a `const`, or a `static` is not.

span.description: A half-open byte range of the pristine file.

target.description: What one target's guards recorded, and which of its tests ran to record it.

reached.description: The mutant sites each test reached.

bodies.description: The branch bodies each test entered, by the index of the marker at the body's first statement.

infected.description: The mutations each test saw its guard's two branches differ over.

entered.description: The items whose bodies each test entered, by item index.

ran.description: Every test the baseline ran, which is what a report nothing could attribute is about.

seen.description: One kind of thing the guards report, by the thread that reported it.

tests.description: What each named test of this target reported, as dense catalog indices (item indices in `entered`).

loose.description: What was reported where nothing named a test, which is therefore about every test of the target.
